You are a financial-analysis assistant working on JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s 2013 annual report extract shown below.  Carefully read the narrative, decide what information you still need, and call the available tools to retrieve it.  Combine tool results with your own reasoning to answer the final question with a single, concrete value (no explanations, no additional text).

Scenario description (excerpt of Management’s Discussion and Analysis):
---------------------------------------------------------------------
management 2019s discussion and analysis 138 jpmorgan chase & co./2013 annual report the credit derivatives used in credit portfolio management activities do not qualify for hedge accounting under u.s .
gaap ; these derivatives are reported at fair value , with gains and losses recognized in principal transactions revenue .
in contrast , the loans and lending-related commitments being risk-managed are accounted for on an accrual basis .
this asymmetry in accounting treatment , between loans and lending-related commitments and the credit derivatives used in credit portfolio management activities , causes earnings volatility that is not representative , in the firm 2019s view , of the true changes in value of the firm 2019s overall credit exposure .
...
credit portfolio hedges the following discussion sets out the fair value related to the firm 2019s credit derivatives used in credit portfolio management activities , the fair value related to the cva ( which reflects the credit quality of derivatives counterparty exposure ) , as well as certain other hedges used in the risk management of cva .
these results can vary from period-to- period due to market conditions that affect specific positions in the portfolio .
net gains and losses on credit portfolio hedges year ended december 31 , ( in millions ) 2013 2012 2011 hedges of loans and lending- related commitments ...

(Only the narrative text is provided; the numerical table has been stored in a database you can query through the tools.)

Available tools
---------------
get_year_id(fiscal_year: int) -> int
    Return the internal database identifier for a given fiscal year.

get_category_id(category_name: str) -> int
    Return the internal identifier for a hedge category (case-insensitive match).

get_hedge_value_millions(year_id: int, category_id: int) -> float
    Fetch the hedge value, in millions, for the given year & category identifiers.

sum_numbers(numbers: List[float]) -> float
    Arithmetic sum of a list of numbers.

percentage(part: float, whole: float, absolute: bool = True) -> float
    Compute what percentage “part” represents of “whole”.  If absolute is True, sign is ignored.

list_categories_by_portfolio_group(group: str) -> List[str]
    List hedge category names for a portfolio group (credit/market/operational).

get_total_counterparty_exposure() -> float
    Aggregate exposure across counterparties (not required for the main task).

get_random_hedge_adjustment(value_id: int) -> float
    Retrieve a random accounting adjustment for a hedge value (irrelevant for the main task).

Question
--------
In 2013, what percent of the total “hedges of loans and lending-related commitments” was represented by “CVA and hedges of CVA”?

Instructions
------------
1. Decide which tools will give you the needed year and category IDs, then obtain the hedge values in millions for each category for 2013.
2. Calculate the total of those two hedge figures.
3. Express the CVA figure as a percentage of that total (use absolute values so that negative signs do not affect the percentage).
4. Round to the nearest whole percent and answer with the number followed by a percent sign, e.g. "48%".
5. Provide only the final answer.
